mistake_content: Missing mandatory module-level configuration 'pytest.app_info = "HPX"' after imports. According to HPX QE QAMA scripting best practices (Pattern A for HPX printer feature tests), this configuration line is MANDATORY and must be placed at module level after imports and before the test class definition. The comment at line 5 indicates '# GLOBAL MISTAKE: Missing pytest.app_info = "HPX" here'. This configuration is critical because: (1) It tells the framework which app to test (HPX vs DESKTOP), (2) The install_app fixture checks pytest.default_info for package resolution, where pytest.default_info is resolved as: if app_info == "DESKTOP" then set_info else app_info, (3) It's required for proper app installation and driver initialization in HPX printer feature tests. Without this configuration, the test framework cannot properly identify and install the correct HPX application package.
solution:
Add the module-level configuration line 'pytest.app_info = "HPX"' immediately after the import statements and before the test class definition. This should be placed at line 6 (after imports, before any test class or fixture definitions). 

Example placement:
```python
import pytest
from MobileApps.libs.flows.android.smart.flow_container import FLOW_NAMES
import time
import logging

pytest.app_info = "HPX"

class Test_Suite_01_Add_Shortcut(object):
    # test methods follow
```

This follows the HPX automation knowledge base Pattern A for printer feature tests, as documented in Level 3a: tests/windows/hpx_rebranding/print/conftest.py. The RULE states: 'When writing a new test for PRINTER features, use Pattern A (HPX).' This configuration ensures the install_app fixture correctly resolves pytest.default_info to 'HPX' for proper package installation and test execution.

mistake_content: Test method 'test_03_verify_the_position_of_the_buttons_on_the_cancel_shortcut_creation_pop_up_window_C48' is missing its required docstring. According to HPX QE QAMA Scripting Best Practice Knowledge Base section 7.1 TEST FILE ANATOMY, all test methods MUST have docstrings containing: (1) a description of what the test verifies, and (2) a TestRails URL in the format 'TestRails -> https://hp-testrail.external.hp.com/index.php?/cases/view/<ID>'. Currently, the test only has a comment '# LOCAL MISTAKE: Missing docstring with TestRail URL' instead of proper documentation.
solution:
Add the required docstring to test_03_verify_the_position_of_the_buttons_on_the_cancel_shortcut_creation_pop_up_window_C48 following the HPX automation framework standard format from section 7.1. The docstring must be placed immediately after the method definition and must include both the test description and TestRails URL. Replace the comment with the following docstring:

```python
def test_03_verify_the_position_of_the_buttons_on_the_cancel_shortcut_creation_pop_up_window_C48(self):
    """
    Verify the buttons of cancel shortcut creation pop up window.
    
    TestRails -> https://hp-testrail.external.hp.com/index.php?/cases/view/48
    """
```

This format ensures compliance with the HPX automation framework's documentation standards, enabling proper test traceability to TestRail case ID 48 and providing clear test intent for maintainability.

solution:
Remove the 'autouse=True' parameter from the class_setup fixture decorator. The correct fixture declaration should be:

```python
@pytest.fixture(scope="class")
def class_setup(self, request, ...):
```

According to the HPX framework knowledge base, class-level setup fixtures should NOT use autouse=True unless they are specifically designed for automatic cleanup operations (like class_initial_cleanup in conftest.py). The standard pattern for test class fixtures is:

```python
@pytest.fixture(scope="class")
def class_setup(cls, <fixtures>):
    cls = cls.__class__
    cls.driver = <driver_source>
    cls.fc = <FlowContainer_source>
    cls.<flow_alias> = cls.fc.fd["<flow_key>"]
```

The autouse parameter causes the fixture to run automatically for all tests in the class, which can lead to unintended side effects and conflicts with the HPX fixture chain. Class setup fixtures should be explicitly invoked through fixture dependencies or usefixtures decorator when needed.

Add the TestRail case ID suffix '_C49' to the test method name. The correct method name should be:

```python
def test_04_verify_the_screen_when_the_user_clicks_on_go_back_button_C49(self):
```

According to the HPX framework naming conventions (Section 20 of the knowledge base), all test methods must include the TestRail case ID suffix in the format '_C<testrail_id>'. The standard pattern is:

```python
@pytest.mark.<marker>
def test_XX_<description>_C<testrail_id>(self):
    """
    <Description of what this test verifies.>
    
    TestRails -> https://hp-testrail.external.hp.com/index...
    """
```

The TestRail case ID suffix is mandatory for test tracking, reporting, and integration with the TestRail test management system. Without this suffix, the test cannot be properly linked to its corresponding test case in TestRail, breaking traceability and automated reporting workflows.
